title: Alpha decay and quantum tunnelling
summary: Nuclides decay by β, α, fission or nucleon emission; an α particle escapes by tunnelling through the Coulomb barrier, which sets the half-life exponentially.

concepts.label: Nuclide
concepts.description: An atomic nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons, in its ground state.

children.label: Half-life
children.description: Time for half of a sample to decay (s).

children.label: Decay mode
children.description: β−, β+/EC, α, fission, p or n emission.

children.label: Proton emission
children.description: Also tunnels through a Coulomb barrier, with Z_α = 1.

children.label: Binding energy per nucleon
children.description: keV per nucleon; peaks near iron, so heavy nuclei gain energy by shedding α particles.

children.label: Nucleon pairing
children.description: Even–even, odd A, odd–odd: unpaired nucleons hinder α decay.

concepts.label: Quantum tunnelling
concepts.description: A particle crossing a barrier higher than its energy, with probability exp(−2G).

facts.text: Gamow, and independently Gurney and Condon, explained α decay by tunnelling in 1928.

children.label: Coulomb barrier
children.description: From the nuclear radius R to the turning point b = 2Z_d e²/(4πε₀Q).

children.label: Preformation factor
children.description: The chance an α cluster exists in the nucleus; not in this model.

concepts.label: Geiger–Nuttall law
concepts.description: log t½ is linear in Z/√Q for each element's isotopes.

concepts.label: Decay chain
concepts.description: Successive decays from ²³⁸U, ²³⁵U or ²³²Th to lead.
